taxonomyNote: NatureServe names it Northern Map Turtle.
fieldMarks: Carapace olive or grayish brown with yellow-orange map-like lines bordered in dark; markings fade with age.
Broad carapace with a moderately low keel and slightly scalloped rear edge.
Head, neck and limbs dark with thin yellow, green or orange stripes, usually with an oval spot behind the eye.
Females much larger (7-10.5 in) than males (3.5-6.5 in); males have narrower heads, longer front claws and thicker tails.
behavior: Avid baskers, often in groups, and very wary: slips into the water at the slightest alarm.
Dormant about November to early April, wedged under submerged logs, in bottom mud or in burrows.
Females eat mainly mollusks and crayfish; males more insectivorous.
habitat: Slow rivers and lakes with mud bottoms, basking logs and abundant aquatic vegetation; also mill ponds and oxbows. Basks on logs and muskrat houses.
range: Southwestern Quebec, southern Ontario and northwestern Vermont to central Minnesota, south through the Mississippi drainage to Arkansas, northern Alabama and eastern Tennessee, west to eastern Kansas; Ohio River drainage; isolated populations in the Delaware, Susquehanna and Hudson drainages.

lookalikes.name: False map turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Lines form a web on the shell and a backward L behind the eye.

lookalikes.name: Ouachita map turtle
lookalikes.howToTell: Large blotch below the eye and dark-ringed blotches on the scutes.
